Exploring Level 2 Autism Spectrum Disorder

Level 2 Autism Spectrum Disorder is clinically classified as 'requiring substantial support.' Individuals with Level 2 autism show noticeable differences in verbal and non-verbal communication, social interaction, and adapting to change. At eMbrace, we focus on building communication tools, expanding independence, and supporting sensory regulation.

Core Traits of Level 2 Autism

  • Communication Differences: Simple verbal sentences, specialized communication styles, or relying on visual aids.
  • Noticeable Social Differences: Difficulty interacting with peers, showing unique social cues even with support.
  • Transition Hurdles: Strong distress or difficulty changing focuses, coping with schedule disruptions, or changing tasks.
  • Repetitive Behaviors: Frequent motor stims, rigid routines, and intense sensory fixations that are central to daily life.

Integrated Therapeutic Approaches at eMbrace

We combine speech therapy (using visual aids and communication tools), occupational therapy (for sensory integration and daily living skills), and parent training to create a supportive, consistent environment at home.

Frequently Asked Questions

We focus on building functional communication, which may include verbal training, visual schedules, picture exchange systems (PECS), or communication software (AAC).

Creating predictable daily routines, using visual planners, designing quiet sensory areas, and maintaining consistent communication strategies are key steps.

Wondering whether an assessment is actually needed?

Our early-signs screener profiles four behaviour clusters separately — attention, impulsivity, social communication, and routines and sensory needs — and weighs how much daily life is affected. You get a straight answer on whether to book, plus a free guide to what an assessment involves and a school accommodations letter template.
